prompt: Design a digital-signature format for offline software release manifests. A manifest includes product, channel, version, artifact digest, minimum compatible version, expiration, and signing-key ID and may be generated by different implementations. Specify the exact canonical bytes that are signed, approved signature algorithm/key form, domain/context separation so a signature cannot authorize another message type, key/algorithm identifier handling, verification order, version/rollback/expiration semantics, and migration to a future signing algorithm. Reject ambiguous serialization, unknown algorithms, malformed signatures, wrong-key/domain/version, modified artifact digests, and downgrade attempts. HSM custody and signing-key rotation ceremony belong to secrets-key-management; this skill owns the signed protocol/verification semantics.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The signed bytes are specified unambiguously and produce identical canonical representation across supplied implementations for semantically identical manifests.
The signature input binds a release-manifest domain/context plus product/channel/version/artifact meaning so a valid signature cannot be transplanted to another protocol message or release context.

Verification checks supported algorithm/key identity, signature authenticity, and authenticated manifest fields before any release/rollback decision trusts them; unknown or attacker-selected downgrade algorithms fail closed.
Version, minimum-version, expiration, and artifact digest rules are explicit and cryptographically covered, with negative fixtures for rollback, expiry, mutation, and wrong artifact.
Algorithm migration is versioned so old/new verifiers have deterministic acceptance rules without silently accepting a weaker unknown/fallback algorithm.
